done_when: forge next lists every other item and names the worktree whose settings it can't read with the refusal's reason, and a test through forge next shows it

findings.body: Running `forge next` from the worktree with rejected settings still prints nothing. This catch converts the refusal into an item line, but `_report` then calls `repo.config(top)` at `src/forge/nextstep.py:143`; because `top` is that same worktree, the refusal escapes before `next_step` prints the report. The new test invokes `forge next` only from the healthy main checkout (`tests/test_fix_one_worktree_with_settings_the_installed.py:27`), so it misses this case. Handle that configuration refusal as an item diagnostic and test the command from the rejected worktree.
